candidates.name: Lamplight
candidates.why: The warm light a patient hand leaves burning while something old is made new.

candidates.name: Sunlit Stone
candidates.why: Old stone in late sun, warm and unhurried, the color of a thing that has been kept well.

candidates.name: Vani Hoard
candidates.why: The granulated gold found at Vani, kept safe in the earth, and the first thing I picture when I think of home.

candidates.name: Willow Leaf
candidates.why: A young willow leaf in spring, going from dull to bright under a patient hand.

candidates.name: Meadow Grass
candidates.why: Meadow grass after rain, where the herbs I gather grow before the moon finds them.

candidates.name: Moonwort
candidates.why: The herb I gather by moonlight, and the freshness a dry branch takes on as I stir it.

candidates.name: Peat Smoke
candidates.why: The dark bog I keep my fires in, with the smoke still hanging over it like a warning to the brave.

candidates.name: Forest Floor
candidates.why: Where the broom never reaches, the rot and the fallen leaves keep their own dark counsel.

candidates.name: Izba Wood
candidates.why: My hut's logs, gone black at the joints from a hundred winters of stove smoke and mischief.

candidates.name: Overcast
candidates.why: The lid of cloud I fly beneath, low and grey, and not a single wand in sight.

candidates.name: Swept Path
candidates.why: The broom takes my tracks off the road behind me, and the dust it leaves is the color of what it hides.

candidates.name: Thyme Bundle
candidates.why: Thyme tied in a bunch and hung to dry under the kitchen beams is this green, gone a little dim with keeping.

candidates.name: Hedgerow
candidates.why: A late-summer hedge, dark and faintly yellow where the light gets through the leaves.

candidates.name: Nettle Cloth
candidates.why: Cloth spun by hand from nettle stems, a green that once stung and now keeps you warm.

candidates.name: Morning Dew
candidates.why: The pale green a garden wears before the sun has had time to dry it.

candidates.name: Willow Mist
candidates.why: Willow leaves seen through early mist, quiet and a little silvered.

candidates.name: Moonwort
candidates.why: An old herbal's silver-green fern, the one that grows only where the moon has been.

candidates.name: Velvet Night
candidates.why: Night wrapped in cloth, dark enough to hold one warm lamp.

candidates.name: Moonless Hour
candidates.why: The hour after the last lamp goes out, when the blue is deepest.

candidates.name: Under Narikala
candidates.why: The fortress wall at night, where the lamps begin behind the carved balconies.

candidates.name: Sugar Cube
candidates.why: A pale, warm white that looks as though it was set down under a lamp.

candidates.name: Lantern Paper
candidates.why: The soft glow of a paper lantern before it is lit, nearly neutral and warm.

candidates.name: Old Plaster
candidates.why: Tbilisi walls gone pale with age, catching the light behind the balconies.

candidates.name: Hoarfrost
candidates.why: Fine frost laid over still air, the palest thing in the room and never cloying.

candidates.name: First Snowfall
candidates.why: The first snow settles on the glass and hushes everything beneath it.

candidates.name: Gergeti Snow
candidates.why: Morning light off the glacier above Gergeti, exact and cool and quietly dazzling.

candidates.name: Frozen Lake
candidates.why: A lake gone still under ice at dusk, clear and cold with nothing warm left in it.

candidates.name: Winter Dusk
candidates.why: The hour when the snow dims to a soft hush and the last light leaves the ridge.

candidates.name: Ice Palace
candidates.why: My own hall seen from outside at dusk, glittering and cold and perfectly still.

candidates.name: Sealing Wax
candidates.why: A seal pressed hard and bold enough to mean it.

candidates.name: Lingonberry
candidates.why: Tart and wild, a berry that dares you to taste it.

candidates.name: Tusheti Fire
candidates.why: The fire kept burning through the highland winter, wild and warm.

candidates.name: Kiln Glow
candidates.why: A little dangerous and warm all the way through, like the glow of a kiln at night.

candidates.name: Qvevri
candidates.why: The clay jars Georgia has buried its wine in for thousands of years, fierce and kind.

candidates.name: Book Cloth
candidates.why: The dark cover of a book I have closed and mean to open again.

candidates.name: Morning Light
candidates.why: Early sun across a page, the first light any good story needs.

candidates.name: Uncut Page
candidates.why: The untrimmed leaf of a new book, the one I most want to turn.

candidates.name: Baked Crust
candidates.why: The crust a loaf wears when the peel draws it from the oven, the colour the bread picks for itself.

candidates.name: Hearth Tile
candidates.why: A tile the fire has warmed, giving its glow back long after the flame has gone.

candidates.name: Qvevri Jar
candidates.why: The potter's qvevri, fired clay that a Georgian cellar keeps its wine in.

candidates.name: Oak Bark
candidates.why: Weathered oak bark, the rough skin of wood that has been working for years.

candidates.name: Garden Soil
candidates.why: The dark soil a spade turns over, rich with the work of the season before.

candidates.name: Carved Balcony
candidates.why: A Tbilisi balcony carved by hand and darkened by decades of weather.

candidates.name: Root Cellar
candidates.why: The cool, earth-dark brown of a cellar's old timber, rarely touched by light.

candidates.name: Pinecone
candidates.why: A pinecone left out through a dry autumn, its brown gone dull and warm.

candidates.name: Gelati Beams
candidates.why: Old roof beams from Gelati, the Georgian thread I keep returning to in my own work.

candidates.name: Lamp Soot
candidates.why: The carbon old scribes scraped from their lamps to make their ink.

candidates.name: Cobblestone
candidates.why: Worn street stones, a steady gray that steps back and lets the picture speak.

candidates.name: Rainy Courtyard
candidates.why: Wet paving after a shower, a calm middle tone that sits quietly under the painting.

candidates.name: Tbilisi Stone
candidates.why: The old stone of a Tbilisi courtyard wall, my own quiet street from the Georgian thread.

candidates.name: Sunlit Plaster
candidates.why: Pale plaster in morning sun, a clean wall that never competes with the picture.

candidates.name: Feather
candidates.why: Barely there and soft, the lightest page in the book, restraint you can hold.

candidates.name: Tbilisi Morning
candidates.why: First light on a Tbilisi courtyard wall, the quiet I hope every painter finds.

candidates.name: Blossom Dust
candidates.why: The faint powder that drifts off the trees when the wind comes through my window in spring.

candidates.name: Dawn Petal
candidates.why: The first soft light on a petal, the way the sky in a picture book wakes up slowly.

candidates.name: Pillowcase
candidates.why: The pillowcase my head sinks into every night, soft and faintly rosy from the wash.

candidates.name: Lamplight
candidates.why: The warm square of light on the ceiling while someone reads me one more page.

candidates.name: Beeswax
candidates.why: The pale wax of the little candle we light for the last story of the night.

candidates.name: Nightlight
candidates.why: The small glow that stays on in the hall so the dark feels friendly and far away.

candidates.name: Glacier Lake
candidates.why: Meltwater over pale rock makes lakes this steady mid-teal, and the name stays out of the way.

candidates.name: Tidewater
candidates.why: The water where the tide turns, clear and steady in this same mid-teal.

candidates.name: Meltwater
candidates.why: The melt in my furnace and the cold snowmelt running down through Tbilisi, one teal to me.

candidates.name: Morning Mist
candidates.why: The first hour over the water, before the color has fully arrived.

candidates.name: Breaker Foam
candidates.why: The lace at a wave's edge, a shade lighter than the water beneath it.

candidates.name: Cold Glass
candidates.why: The faint tint of thin glass held to the light before a piece leaves the bench.

candidates.name: Chimney Soot
candidates.why: The black above the hearth, where the bread stays warm all night.

candidates.name: Cold Hearth
candidates.why: What the fire leaves at dawn, still warm to the hand.

candidates.name: Oilcloth Night
candidates.why: The black oilcloth my pictures sit on, under every feast I painted.

candidates.name: Bread Crust
candidates.why: The golden top of the bread my mother pulls from the tonir.

candidates.name: Sunbaked Loaf
candidates.why: A flatbread left on the feast table at noon, baked by the sun and by love.

candidates.name: Tonir Wall
candidates.why: The clay oven's side in our courtyard, colored by a hundred baking days.

candidates.name: Milk Glass
candidates.why: Opaque as a pitcher on the pantry shelf, warm at the edges the way old paper is.

candidates.name: Herbarium Paper
candidates.why: The sheet I pressed my summer on, kept folded in the drawer where the flowers still are.

candidates.name: Gloaming
candidates.why: The hour the garden goes to a quieter room, and I stop at the door to watch it.

candidates.name: Moorland Dusk
candidates.why: Heath gone soft at evening, the shade of a thing remembered rather than seen.

candidates.name: Winter Afternoon
candidates.why: The slant of light I write by in December, when every shadow goes faintly to dusk.

candidates.name: Sealing Wax
candidates.why: Pressed into warm wax, this deep, glossy red is the mark that says whose work this is.

candidates.name: Velvet Drape
candidates.why: I think of the heavy curtain on a shared stage: deep, generous, and open for everyone to see.

candidates.name: Banked Embers
candidates.why: Banking the fire overnight so the next person can light their own from it is how I think of sharing.

candidates.name: Paper Lantern
candidates.why: Lit from within, it gives this same soft coral glow to a room anyone can walk into.

candidates.name: Sunlit Plaster
candidates.why: A warm wall in late sun turns this soft coral, like the old walls where many hands have left their marks.

candidates.name: Torchlight
candidates.why: Passed hand to hand so every traveler sees the road, the way open work lights the path for those who follow.

candidates.name: Night Ferry
candidates.why: A small boat crossing dark water with a lantern lit, steered by someone who means well.

candidates.name: Small Hours
candidates.why: The hours after midnight, when I wake and walk the corridor to make sure the child is safe.

candidates.name: Old Varnish
candidates.why: The glow of a wooden toy loved for years and rubbed to a shine by small hands.

candidates.name: Puppet Wood
candidates.why: The carved wood of the puppets who play out their lives beneath the old clock tower in Tbilisi.

candidates.name: First Light
candidates.why: Dawn light on an empty stage, moving before the music has even started.

candidates.name: Pointe Shoe
candidates.why: Every studio I worked in had these pink satin shoes, lifting a dancer's whole weight into one clean line.

candidates.name: Evening Sea
candidates.why: The sea at dusk moves in unhurried phrases, paced like an adagio.

candidates.name: Kura River
candidates.why: The Kura runs fast through Tbilisi, and speed and pride are the Georgian in me.

candidates.name: Still Water
candidates.why: A lake at evening, so quiet you can hear the guitar from the far shore.

candidates.name: Evening Sea
candidates.why: The sea goes this color when the day is tired and nobody has much left to say.

candidates.name: Arbat Dusk
candidates.why: The Arbat at nightfall, lamps not yet lit, somebody singing behind an open window.

candidates.name: Barley Field
candidates.why: The field at the end of a long day, the harvest in and the people walking home slowly.

candidates.name: Late Light
candidates.why: The sun low over the roofs, a light that asks nothing of anyone.

candidates.name: Courtyard Lamp
candidates.why: The one lamp still burning in the courtyard, where the neighbors leave their windows open.
